content: This product is not guaranteed to be safe, effective, or suitable for your use. The information provided here is not personalized medical advice and should not replace the guidance of your healthcare professional. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. To apply eye medication, first wash your hands thoroughly. Avoid wearing contact lenses if you have an eye infection or while using this medication. Tilt your head back, look upward, and gently pull down the lower eyelid to create a small pouch. Hold the dropper directly above your eye and place one drop into the pouch. Look downward, gently close your eyes, and place one finger at the inner corner of your eye (near the nose). Apply gentle pressure for 1 to 2 minutes before opening your eyes to prevent the medication from draining out. Avoid blinking or rubbing your eyes. Do not rinse the dropper after use. If you are using another type of eye medication (such as drops or ointments), wait at least 5 minutes between applications. Use this medication regularly to achieve the best results. To help you remember, use it at the same times each day. Continue using this medication for the full duration prescribed, even if your symptoms improve after a few days. Temporary blurred vision and mild eye irritation or redness may occur after applying this medication. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before using ganciclovir, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to valganciclovir, or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. After applying this medication, your vision may become temporarily blurred. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. It is unknown if this drug passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription drugs, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. If someone has overdosed and is experiencing serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Laboratory and/or medical tests (such as eye exams) may be performed while you are using this medication. Keep all medical and lab appointments. If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and use your next dose at the regular time. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature and protect it from freezing. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in May 2024. It is a summary and does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
